newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast product prices steady to lower late.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast product prices steady to lower late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices steadied or fell slightly with technical pressure from NYMEX curbed by bullish fundamentals.
"I would be surprised if this trend continues," one broker said, referring to profit-taking that came on the heels of a 1.74-cent fall in October NYMEX gasoline Thursday.
The front-month ended at 61.32 cents a gallon amid concerns about imports and higher stocks.
Locally, traders saw more upward pressure near-term with gasoline stocks at signficant lows of 26.9 million and cutbacks expected in production for autumn maintenance.

Traders heard rumours of a possible deal between Ultramar and Powerine refinery, located in Santa Fe Springs, California. Under the rumoured terms, Ultramar would own crude and gasoline which mothballed Powerine would process for a fee.
Conventional or "clear" grade gasoline in Los Angeles fell a cent to 65/66 cents a gallon. Discounts for San Francisco grade widened a half cent to hit 2.50 cents below L.A. material.
And Premium conventional in L.A. was nine cents over regular on ongoing problems with key Mobil gasoline unit, and new rumours of a possible reformer problem with a Texaco plant.
CARB gasoline in L.A. stayed 70.50/71 cents a gallon.
Bids for CARB diesel in L.A. were flat at 76/77 with low sulphur at off about a cent to 70.50/71.50 cents.
Distillates are expected to soften, with cargoes expected soon.
